head_commit.message:
Manage TUI backend sessions independently (#55381)

## What changed

Add a `BackendSessions` collection to own app-server sessions and poll their events fairly with cancellation-safe receives. Track listening state per backend so pausing or closing one stream leaves the others available, and resume polling after reconnect. Shut down all registered sessions on exit.

Ignore background backend disconnect, lag, account, and rate-limit events that would otherwise update the displayed conversation's UI.

## Testing

Add coverage for polling three sessions, paused and closed stream isolation, cancellation, and session replacement after reconnect. Extend event ownership coverage to verify that background lifecycle and account events leave the displayed connection and rate-limit state untouched.

Handle response body failures in OpenAI docs downloads (#55379)

## Why

Response body reads could outlive the manual download timeout or fail outside the existing fallback and retry handlers.

## What changed

- Read successful manual response bodies within the fetch timeout and transport fallback so stalled or failed reads fall back to `curl`. Leave `HEAD` responses unconsumed.
- Await model metadata response bodies inside the retry handler so read failures use the existing three-attempt retry loop.

## Testing

Add regression tests for manual body timeouts and truncated bodies falling back to `curl` before caching, plus model metadata body failures succeeding on retry or stopping after three attempts. All four tests pass with `node --test codex-rs/skills/tests/openai_docs_downloads.test.mjs`.

head_commit.message:
Preserve thread metadata before rollout files are materialized (#55380)

## Why

A live thread can have updated SQLite metadata before its rollout file exists.
Reading metadata from the missing file loses creation details such as fork and
parent relationships and triggers unnecessary filesystem discovery and retries.

## What changed

- Read deferred `SessionMeta` through the rollout writer, ordered with persistence.
  Return no in-memory metadata once the rollout is materialized or resumed.
- Combine that creation metadata with SQLite metadata for reads that exclude
  history, and use it to determine the canonical history mode during updates.
- Keep untouched threads without a stored record unavailable for fork and resume.

## Testing

Add coverage for metadata reads and updates before persistence in both legacy and
paginated history modes, including equality with metadata read after persistence.
Verify the recorder exposes creation metadata only while deferred, and expand
fork/resume rejection tests across history modes and resume turn inclusion.

head_commit.message:
Add configured thread environment inheritance for subagents (#55375)

## Why

Temporary environment attachments for a parent turn should not become a
subagent's persistent environments. Children also need to retain their
configured executor bindings when their runtime is evicted and reloaded.

## What changed

- Add the disabled-by-default `subagent_thread_environments` feature flag.
  When enabled, both subagent implementations inherit configured thread
  environments captured with the invoking step, excluding turn-only attachments.
- Track configured bindings separately from active turn attachments, preserving
  pending configuration ownership and sharing completed executor startup.
- Retain configured selections and bindings across idle eviction. Reload children
  using retained bindings when the parent changes workspace, while continuing to
  validate current parent roots and permissions for matching workspaces.

## Testing

Extend regression coverage for configured, empty, forked, pending, and legacy
inheritance; temporary attachment removal across eviction; and reload behavior
with changed workspaces, deferred startup, and restricted permissions.

GitOrigin-RevId: 15692ecd99deb38002014b44fd859d793bd54373

Command-line initial prompts bypass the composer and were missing from local recall history, so pressing Up could skip them and retrieve cross-session history instead.

Enable incremental tools by default for Responses Lite (#55368)

## What changed

Mark `incremental_tools` as stable and enable it by default. Responses Lite sessions now append tool catalog updates to request history without requiring an explicit feature opt-in.

## Testing

Run the incremental catalog scenario with the default configuration. Update assertions and snapshots for empty Responses Lite prewarm input, tool declarations on the first turn, preserved compaction history, and tool changes across model switches and child agents.
